Loopback0 carries the router-id and the LAN port the site LAN

Traffic through the tunnels is encrypted with the modelled transform set

Routers exist in Nautobot with role, serial, platform and management IP matching reality
WAN links are modelled as cables: spoke port to the headend's firewall, firewall to the headend, /30 addresses
The VPN is modelled in Nautobot's core VPN app: one VPN, one tunnel per hub/spoke pair, hub/spoke endpoints
Locations form the hierarchy lab site -> region -> branch, with site metadata on the branch

Every PSK spoke uses its own pre-shared key on all of its tunnels, each headend keys per PSK spoke and holds no key for a certificate spoke

BGP model: one AS per site, eBGP peerings over the tunnel addresses matching the live sessions

Golden Config: router backups are in Gitea and every compliance row is compliant
Each headend has exactly one firewall, reachable over the OOB network with SSH
Firewall interfaces carry the modelled addresses and face the right neighbours
The rendered firewall configuration matches what runs on the firewalls
Only IKEv2, ESP and ICMP cross the firewall, IKEv2 and ESP only between the modelled WAN addresses; the tunnels actually carry ESP through it
Firewall bandwidth is modelled in Nautobot and bounds the headend capacity together with the tunnel count
Headend CPU is collected live and joins the aggregate capacity
Non-VPN traffic from a spoke to a headend is dropped by the firewall
The firewalls ship their firewall log to VictoriaLogs, and the portal reads the history from there
The lab CA exists and the routers with certificate tunnels trust exactly it, pinned by fingerprint
Every router with a certificate tunnel holds a certificate issued by the lab CA to its own name, valid and not close to expiry; key-only routers hold none
Certificate tunnels authenticate with rsa-sig against the trustpoint; a key stays only where a spoke chose one
The NaC data carries a key only for the spokes that chose one, and the rendered model matches Nautobot
Nautobot records the certificate every router presents
The portal renews a spoke's certificate: new serial on the router, in the CA index and in Nautobot; every tunnel back with RSA
